Appropriate pinned Exomiser configuration without the added model
endpoints: Case-level top-k recovery of independently adjudicated causal findings
Analyst review burden, missed variant classes, unresolved cases and abstention
Confirmed diagnosis measured separately from a ranked candidate

Frozen gene–disease knowledge and model training cutoff
Keep unsolved cases in workload/coverage denominators
Audit evaluation labels for predictor-derived evidence

use_cases.title: Unresolved rare-disease reanalysis
use_cases.user: Clinical genomics service responsible for previously unresolved cases
use_cases.initial_scope: A dated unresolved ES/GS cohort with recorded changes to phenotype, calls and gene–disease knowledge.
use_cases.comparison_question: Does a proposed reanalysis method improve confirmed diagnoses or reduce review burden relative to refreshed conventional analysis using identical updated information?
baselines: Refreshed conventional workflow with the same new knowledge, calls and phenotypes
Original unresolved cohort for programme-level incremental yield, reported separately
endpoints: New confirmed diagnoses per eligible case over a stated interval
Incremental method benefit under equal updated inputs
False alerts, review time and reason for each resolved case
validation_requirements: Separate new-information benefit from algorithmic benefit
Freeze original and update dates
Family/site separation and no future-knowledge leakage
Count diagnoses and diagnosed individuals separately

candidate_sources.role: Exomiser reanalysis implementation; preserve cohort denominators
Talos reanalysis implementation; distinguish 241 diagnoses from 238 people

use_cases.next_deliverable: Dated reanalysis evidence table with separate programme-yield and method-comparison columns.
acceptance_criteria: Capture cohort eligibility and both analysis dates
Attribute changes to knowledge, phenotype, calling or ranking where reported
Identify the refreshed same-input comparator or document its absence
source_constraints: Controlled cohort access may be required for new evaluations; published implementation evidence is not permission to download patient data
